content.value:
A DC motor spins a shaft when you apply power.

In FTC, each motor is controlled by a motor controller that translates your setPower() commands into electrical current.

Power values range from -1.0 (full reverse) to 0.0 (stopped) to 1.0 (full forward).

Most motors also have built-in encoders that count how far they've turned.

The hardwareMap connects your code to the robot's devices.

You ask it for motors, sensors, and servos by name.

steps.title: Where do the names come from?

content.value:
Device names are set in the robot configuration, which you create in the Driver Station app or by editing an XML file.

Common motor names include "front_left_motor", "front_right_motor", "back_left_motor", "back_right_motor".

The name must match exactly.

steps.title: Declare a field for your motor

content.value:
At the class level, add: private DcMotor motor;

Fields declared with private are only accessible within this class. This is good practice.

Inside init(), type motor = hardwareMap.get(DcMotor.class, "front_left_motor");

The first argument is the type of device, the second is the name from the config. Assign it to the motor field.

The hardware map found a motor matching that name and gave you a reference.

You can now control it from anywhere in your OpMode using the motor variable.

You'll use this same pattern for every device: motors, sensors, servos.
